expr: (list (with-temp-buffer (insert "one two. three four") (let ((fill-column 12)) (fill-region (point-min) (point-max)) (buffer-substring (point-min) (point-max)))) (with-temp-buffer (insert "one two. three four") (let ((fill-column 12) (sentence-end-double-space nil)) (fill-region (point-min) (point-max)) (buffer-substring (point-min) (point-max)))))
note:
THE FINDING, and it would have been implemented wrongly from any description of filling as `break at the last space that fits'. Emacs answers ("one
two. three
four" "one two.
three four"). With the DEFAULT `sentence-end-double-space' (t), Emacs REFUSES to end a line just after a period followed by a single space -- that would read as a sentence end where the author wrote an abbreviation -- so it backs the break up to after "one" and produces a SHORTER first line than the column allows. Bind the variable to nil and the same text fills the obvious way. THE DECISION, MADE: kg's `fill-region' does NOT implement the nobreak rule, and this case is a RECORDED DIVERGENCE that stays divergent after F.1 -- kg has no `sentence-end-double-space', no sentence machinery to hang it on, and s-word-wrap's own demand is a column, not a typographic convention. The row exists so that divergence is chosen rather than discovered by whoever first fills a paragraph with a period in it. kg answers `void-function' at this pin.
